title: The geometric phase diagram, diffusion, and spectra of random planar maps
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Random planar maps weighted by FK clusters are discrete models of 2D quantum gravity. For q<=4 they converge to Liouville-quantum-gravity spheres, and for q>4 they converge to a random tree. Random walks on these maps converge to Liouville Brownian motion.
explicit_constants: Partly. The time acceleration equals the number of edges exactly. The distance normalizations are deterministic but unspecified.
opportunity: None. Scaling limits of random surfaces matter to probability and 2D quantum-gravity theory. No computational or engineering workflow depends on them.
caveats: The spectral and Brownian-motion results assume stated LQG/Brownian-map inputs. Lean covers only the q>4 continuum-random-tree limit.

title: Planar first-passage geometry and the absence of bigeodesics
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: In planar first-passage percolation (random edge travel times on Z^2), no doubly infinite geodesic exists. For exponential weights, the asymptotic shape of the reachable set is strictly convex with a smooth (C^1) boundary.
constructive: no: these are structural almost-sure statements
explicit_constants: none
opportunity: None. FPP is a toy model for growth and transport. Practitioners in KPZ-type growth and network routing get no new quantity: the limit shape and time constant are still not computed.
caveats: Lean covers only the Gamma-weight differentiability. Strict convexity is not formalized.

title: Critical percolation on every quasi-transitive graph
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: At exactly the critical density, bond and site percolation on the cubic lattice Z^3 has no infinite cluster. The same holds for bond percolation on every infinite symmetric (quasi-transitive) graph. The percolation transition is therefore continuous.
explicit_constants: none: p_c is not computed, and no exponents or finite-size rates are given
opportunity: None in practice. Modellers of porous media, conductivity in composites and network robustness already assume the 3D transition is continuous and use numerically measured p_c and exponents. This settles a famous open problem without giving them any new number.
caveats: Infinite-volume and qualitative. Says nothing about finite systems or exponents.

title: The Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: On every nonamenable symmetric graph (for example, hyperbolic lattices or free-group Cayley graphs), percolation has a nonempty density range with infinitely many infinite clusters, and the triangle condition holds at criticality.
explicit_constants: none
opportunity: None. Real networks are finite and not quasi-transitive. Hyperbolic random-graph models used in network science are outside the theorem.
caveats: Applies only to infinite quasi-transitive graphs.

title: Canonical O(3) continuum limit and exact O(4) mass asymptotics
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: The 2D lattice Heisenberg model (O(3)) and its O(n) relatives (n>=3) have exponentially decaying correlations (a mass gap) at every temperature. The O(3) continuum limit is a genuine interacting quantum field theory. The square-lattice O(4) mass is pinned exactly: m ~ 32 e^{pi/4-1/2} sqrt(beta) e^{-pi beta}.
constructive: partial: the continuum limit is constructed, but no algorithm is given
explicit_constants: Yes for the O(4) leading prefactor 32e^{pi/4-1/2}. The O(n) decay constants A and m are not explicit.
opportunity: Validation only. The paper frames the O(4) prefactor as identifying the Hasenfratz–Maggiore–Niedermayer exact-mass prediction in lattice units. Lattice Monte Carlo practitioners already use that prediction to check asymptotic scaling of 2D sigma models. Making the mass gap rigorous (a Polyakov-type conjecture, now Lean-formalized for O(n) decay) changes no code or parameter choice.
caveats: The O(4) mass relies on a companion sharp-order paper. Only the O(n) exponential decay is formalized.

title: Critical and near-critical XY scaling and BKT universality
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: For the 2D XY model of planar spins, the critical correlation decays as r^{-1/4}(log r)^{1/8}, and the correlation length has the predicted Kosterlitz–Thouless essential singularity. Related height models converge to Gaussian free fields.
explicit_constants: No: the amplitudes A_XY and B_XY are only shown to be positive and finite.
opportunity: None operational. The log-corrected ansatz is already the standard fitting form in finite-size-scaling Monte Carlo studies of the XY/BKT transition. The amplitudes are not computed, so fits gain no new input.
caveats: The center-magnetization and spin-field results assume stated companion inputs. Nothing is formalized.

title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation law
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Below the spin-glass transition (beta>1), the SK model's log partition function fluctuates on the scale n^{1/6} (variance ~ c n^{1/3}), with a nondegenerate limiting law.
explicit_constants: No: c_beta>0 is unspecified.
opportunity: None. Numerical spin-glass studies debate the ground-state (zero-temperature) fluctuation exponent. This result is at fixed positive temperature and gives no amplitude, so it does not settle that debate or feed any benchmark.
caveats: Fixed beta>1, zero field, Gaussian couplings. Not formalized.

title: Conformal universality for weakly interacting and random-bond Ising models
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Adding weak extra multispin interactions, or weak random bond disorder, to the 2D critical Ising model does not change its conformally invariant scaling limits (SLE_3 interfaces and the bulk spin and energy correlations).
explicit_constants: No: 'sufficiently small' perturbation strengths are not quantified.
opportunity: None. This confirms that weak disorder is irrelevant (the Harris-criterion marginal case) as physicists expect. No numerical or experimental practice changes.
caveats: Perturbation strengths are unquantified. Lean covers only a finite comparison lemma.

title: GOE bulk universality for regular graphs with weak Anderson disorder
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Eigenvalue spacings of a random d-regular graph's adjacency matrix follow random-matrix (GOE) statistics in the bulk, for every fixed d>=3. This persists with weak random on-site potentials.
explicit_constants: No: the disorder strength w_0(d,kappa) is unspecified.
opportunity: None. The Anderson model on random regular graphs is a physics proxy for many-body localization. The theorem covers only weak disorder, far from the localization transition, where numerics already show GOE statistics.
caveats: Weak disorder only. Not formalized.

title: Directional zero–one laws beyond iid environments and iid ballisticity
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: For random walks in random environments on Z^d, escape in a given direction has probability 0 or 1. In iid uniformly elliptic environments, directional transience forces a nonzero limiting speed (ballisticity).
explicit_constants: none
opportunity: None. These are qualitative RWRE dichotomies with no computable velocity and no applied consumer.

title: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: For sparse random spin systems (Viana–Bray, diluted even-p spin, soft even-K SAT) on Poisson random hypergraphs, the free energy equals the infimum of the physicists' hierarchical cavity (replica-symmetry-breaking) formula. Letting temperature go to zero gives the same statement for the optimal objective value per variable.
constructive: partial: a variational formula. Any finite-depth trial gives a rigorous upper bound (already known from Panchenko–Talagrand). Equality holds only in the infimum over all depths, and no algorithm is given.
explicit_constants: No rates. The ground-state value is a double limit (beta->inf of an infimum).
opportunity: Non-obvious channel: the hypotheses (factorization e^theta=a(1+b f f) with E[(-b)^n]>=0) appear to cover the antiferromagnetic Ising model (b=-tanh beta). That is Max-Cut on sparse Poisson/Erdős–Rényi graphs, although the paper's corollary lists only symmetric couplings. The ground-state corollary would then make the limiting sparse-ER Max-Cut density equal the zero-temperature limit of the hierarchical cavity value. Population-dynamics (1RSB and beyond) Max-Cut estimates for benchmarking heuristics, Ising machines and QAOA on sparse random graphs would become rigorously anchored. It is still only an infimum: certified numbers need new computer-assisted work, and most QAOA benchmarks use random regular graphs, not Poisson graphs.
targets: Max-Cut / spin-glass ground-state benchmark literature on sparse random graphs (QAOA, Ising machines, simulated annealing)
cavity/population-dynamics solvers used to produce reference values
first_step: Verify that J≡-1 (antiferromagnet, p=2) satisfies (model:factorization)-(model:positivity) and state the sparse-ER Max-Cut corollary. Then compare published 1RSB Max-Cut estimates to the finite-depth upper bounds.
caveats: Poisson degrees and even arity only (the paper notes this excludes random 3-SAT). Finite-depth upper bounds were already rigorous. The infimum is not shown to be attained at low depth.

title: Perceptron free energies and microscopic jamming exponents
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: This gives exact free-energy formulas for random perceptrons (binary or spherical weights, with bounded soft loss potentials) at every pattern density and positive temperature. It also proves sharp 'jamming' exponents (gamma≈0.41269, theta≈0.42311) for the negative-margin spherical perceptron, which physics uses as a mean-field model of sphere packing.
constructive: partial: explicit variational formulas, plus a finite numerical certificate for the exponent intervals
explicit_constants: The jamming exponents are certified to about 7 digits. The free-energy formulas are variational, with no convergence rates.
opportunity: Theory only. ML theory gets rigorous Gardner-type formulas for soft-loss 'Gibbs learning' of random labels at all densities; earlier rigorous results covered only small density. The certified exponents confirm the Franz–Parisi / Charbonneau et al. jamming predictions. The hard-constraint storage capacity that ML-theory papers usually cite is explicitly excluded, and there is no teacher–student or generalization setting, so practitioners see no change.
first_step: Use the bi-orthogonally invariant spherical formula as a rigorous baseline in structured-data perceptron analyses (no engineering action).
caveats: Positive temperature and bounded potentials only. Capacity (hard constraints) is excluded. Lean covers the spherical formula and only finiteness for the Ising variational value.

title: Random-cluster interfaces: critical, disordered, thermal, and natural-time scaling
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Critical FK random-cluster interfaces on the square lattice converge to SLE_kappa curves and CLE loop ensembles for 0<q<=4. This includes Cardy's crossing formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundaries.
explicit_constants: none (one deterministic normalization constant for natural time)
opportunity: None. Cardy's formula is already used, as a conjecture checked numerically, to validate percolation codes. Making it rigorous for the square lattice changes no simulation practice.
caveats: Not formalized. Some cases require smooth domains.

title: Critical and quenched near-critical universality for Poisson–Voronoi percolation
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: For percolation on a random Voronoi tessellation (randomly colored cells), critical crossing probabilities follow Cardy's conformal formula. Near-critical crossing thresholds match the triangular-lattice law even conditional on the tessellation.
explicit_constants: No: the pivotal amplitude constant is unspecified.
opportunity: None practical. Voronoi percolation models polycrystals and granular composites, but practitioners simulate actual geometries. Exact asymptotic crossing laws at p=1/2 do not alter those workflows.
caveats: The quenched result takes Cardy's formula as an input. Not formalized.

title: Gaussian free field limits throughout the balanced six-vertex regime
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: The height function of the 2D square-ice (six-vertex) model with a=b=1, 0<c<=2 converges to a Gaussian free field with variance multiplier 1/arcsin(c/2).
explicit_constants: Yes: the variance multiplier is exactly 1/arcsin(c/2).
opportunity: None. This confirms a known Bethe-ansatz/Coulomb-gas prediction for an exactly solvable model.
caveats: Not formalized.

title: The double-dimer loop ensemble converges to CLE4
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Overlaying two independent random domino tilings of a Temperleyan square-lattice upper-half-plane domain produces loops that converge to the nested CLE_4 loop ensemble.
explicit_constants: none
opportunity: None.
caveats: Half-plane Temperleyan case only. Not formalized.

title: Critical SK autocorrelation processes and dynamics across the temperature transition
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: For the SK spin glass, single-site heat-bath (Gibbs) sampling behaves as follows. Throughout the high-temperature phase (beta<1) it mixes fast, with a constant spectral gap and cutoff at log n/(2 lambda(beta)). At beta=1 it slows to n^{2/3} per site. For beta>1 it stays far from equilibrium for stretched-exponential time when started from a typical equilibrium state.
constructive: partial: the standard Glauber sampler is certified, but the rate constants are implicit
explicit_constants: No: lambda(beta) satisfies only 0<lambda<=(1-beta)^2, and C_beta is unspecified. The beta>1 barrier time exp(n^{1/10000}) and upper bound exp(n^{1-1/4e7}) are useless at simulable n.
opportunity: This extends rigorous fast-mixing guarantees for SK Gibbs sampling from beta<1/2 (+eps; Wang 2026, Boban–Li–Oveis Gharan) to the whole high-temperature phase. It also quantifies critical slowing down: n^{5/3} single-site attempts at beta=1. That is a qualitative certificate for high-temperature replicas in parallel-tempering ladders and for Gibbs samplers on dense Gaussian couplings. Constants are implicit, the results hold in probability over Gaussian disorder at zero field, and the low-temperature barriers are galactic, so no practitioner changes burn-in or ladder design.
targets: MCMC theory for Ising / Boltzmann-machine Gibbs samplers
first_step: Estimate lambda(beta) empirically for n<=10^4 and test whether log n/(2 lambda) predicts observed burn-in. If it does, cite the theorem in temperature-ladder heuristics.
caveats: Zero field and Gaussian disorder, in probability. Cutoff is formalized only for beta<1/2. Algorithmic stochastic localization already samples SK in parts of this range.

title: Continuum phase transitions for radial pair potentials
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: This constructs stable, distance-dependent pair potentials for 3D classical particles whose free energy has a first-order (kink) temperature singularity over a range of densities. It answers Simon's continuum phase-transition problem for engineered radial potentials.
constructive: partial: the potential is constructed, but its core scale e^{-t} uses an unspecified 'sufficiently large' t
explicit_constants: beta_c lies in [7/8,9/8] and the density interval is centred at 5p/3. The construction parameter t is not explicit.
opportunity: None. The potential is engineered with a microscopic core at scale e^{-t} for unspecified large t, so it cannot even be simulated in LAMMPS/HOOMD. The question that matters to molecular simulation, whether realistic potentials like Lennard-Jones have transitions, remains open.
caveats: Existence proof for an artificial interaction.
evidence: /root/openai-math/preprints/A-radial-continuum-phase-transition-with-algebraic-decay-September-24-2026/build/sections/introduction.tex (Thm thm:main); foundations.tex (core psi_t, t sufficiently large)

title: Exact three- and four-state reconstruction thresholds and four-state tree capacity
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: When a 3-state (either sign) or assortative 4-state symbol is broadcast down a tree through a noisy symmetric channel, the root can be recovered from far-away leaves exactly when d·lambda^2>1 (the Kesten–Stigum bound), for every degree. Consequently, 3 symmetric communities in a sparse stochastic block model can be weakly recovered iff (a-b)^2 > 3(a+2b).
constructive: partial: the impossibility side is information-theoretic, and achievability reuses the existing O(n log n) Abbe–Sandon algorithm. The proofs are computer-assisted, with exact-arithmetic C++/Python verifiers shipped.
explicit_constants: Yes: the thresholds are exact (d·lambda^2=1; SBM (a-b)^2=3(a+2b)).
opportunity: This certifies at every average degree the KS reference line that community-detection benchmarks (BP, non-backtracking spectral, line-graph GNN papers) plot against for q=3; previously only large degree was proven (Mossel–Sly–Sohn 2025). Non-obvious BIO channel: the ferromagnetic 4-state channel is exactly the Jukes–Cantor substitution model. The root (ancestral) state of a deep d-ary tree, including binary trees, is therefore unrecoverable exactly when per-branch change probability p >= (3/4)(1-1/sqrt d), about 0.22 for d=2. This pins the KS phase transition used in phylogenetic sequence-length theory. Both uses confirm what practitioners already assumed.
targets: community-detection benchmark suites and papers using SBM KS threshold curves
phylogenetic reconstruction theory (Jukes–Cantor ancestral reconstruction / sequence-length phase transitions)
first_step: Cite the exact q=3 SBM threshold (and the q=4 assortative tree threshold) as the proven reference line in SBM benchmark generators and surveys. Note in phylogenetics theory surveys that KS-sharpness for Jukes–Cantor on regular and Poisson trees is now a (computer-assisted) theorem.
caveats: Lean formalizes only the classical supercritical direction. The new non-reconstruction direction is unformalized and computer-assisted. The 4-state result is tree-only; an assortative 4-community SBM corollary likely follows via the same transfer but is not stated. Equal branch lengths and equal-size communities only.

title: Exact Hausdorff gauges for SLE
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: This finds the exact fine-scale size function r^d (log log 1/r)^{(2-d)/2} that gives SLE_kappa curves positive and finite Hausdorff measure.
explicit_constants: Yes: the gauge is explicit.
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean covers the lower bound (positivity).

title: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: The free uniform spanning forest on any infinite graph can be generated from independent per-vertex random labels by one symmetric rule that needs no root. The same holds for invariant strongly Rayleigh and determinantal processes on countable groups.
constructive: no: Borel and non-finitary (Brownian-path/SDE readout via limsups), with no coding radius
explicit_constants: none
opportunity: None. The construction reads out a limsup of infinitely many Brownian paths and has no finitary coding radius, so it gives no local or parallel sampler. Practical spanning-tree and DPP sampling (Wilson's algorithm, spectral DPP samplers) is untouched.
caveats: Infinite graphs and groups only.

title: Gaussian fields and interfaces for triangular-lattice Lipschitz heights
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Random Lipschitz height functions on the triangular lattice converge to Gaussian free fields. Their zero-level interface at a tuned boundary converges to SLE_4.
explicit_constants: Partly: an absolutely convergent finite-volume formula for the normalization in one case.
opportunity: None.
caveats: The Lipschitz-height manuscripts were among those repaired on Oct 7 2026. Not formalized.

title: The joint critical Ashkin–Teller current limit
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Along the critical Ashkin–Teller line, including the 4-state Potts endpoint, the height field and current clusters converge jointly to a Gaussian free field and its level-set structures.
explicit_constants: none
opportunity: None.
caveats: The Ashkin–Teller current manuscripts were repaired on Oct 7 2026. Not formalized.

title: All-temperature pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: This gives an exact free-energy formula, at every temperature, for Ising models whose coupling matrix is a Haar-random rotation of a given spectrum (for example, Hopfield/Wishart couplings G^T G). At zero temperature it gives the limiting optimum of max and min sigma^T J sigma over sign vectors, including the Gaussian ||G||_{inf->2} norm and the minimum ||sum sigma_i g_i||.
constructive: partial: a variational formula (infimum over Parisi-type paths, using the edge-extended R-transform) with no algorithm
explicit_constants: No rates. Values require numerically solving the variational problem.
opportunity: This supplies asymptotic optimal values for QUBO on rotationally invariant ensembles: Gaussian-pattern Hopfield/Wishart couplings, the random orthogonal model, and Gaussian vector balancing (min over signs of ||G sigma||). Once solved numerically, these could serve as ground-truth targets for benchmarking Ising machines, QAOA, simulated bifurcation and AMP/OAMP-type optimizers beyond SK, analogous to the Parisi value used in 281. External fields correlated with J, as in planted, CDMA or MIMO detection, are not covered.
targets: Ising-machine / QUBO benchmarking on Hopfield/Wishart instance families
AMP/OAMP/VAMP optimization theory for rotationally invariant matrices
first_step: Numerically solve the zero-temperature formula for Wishart couplings at alpha=1 and compare with simulated-annealing ground states at n≈10^3–10^4.
caveats: No outliers in the spectrum, and the deterministic external fields must have W1-convergent empirical laws. The infimum is not shown to be computable to certified precision.

title: Limiting random SAT thresholds, sharp variance and computability
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Random k-SAT has a sharp limiting satisfiability threshold for every k>=3. The number of clauses at which a growing random 3-SAT formula first becomes unsatisfiable fluctuates by Theta(sqrt n). The 3-SAT threshold is a computable real number, but no efficient way to compute it is given.
constructive: partial: computability is via an unbounded certificate search with no efficiency bound. Lower certificates f_n/n - 2^67 n^{-1/6} are galactic, since they only become nontrivial for n>2^389. Upper certificates are finite rational RSB-type trials that can be evaluated exactly with interval arithmetic.
explicit_constants: Var(H_n)<=Cn with C unspecified. The lower-certificate error is 2^67 n^{-1/6}. The threshold is not evaluated (the paper does not claim 4.267).
opportunity: SAT benchmark generation: Theta(n) variance plus Wilson's lower bound gives a satisfiability window of Theta(sqrt n) clauses, a density window of order n^{-1/2}. That means finite-size-scaling exponent nu=2, contradicting the long-quoted empirical nu≈1.5 for 3-SAT. Generators of 'hard' random 3-SAT near clause/variable ratio 4.26 should expect the window to shrink as n^{-1/2}. The center's n-dependence has no rate, so per-n empirical calibration stays necessary. Secondary: finite rational upper certificates could, with certified interval evaluation of a good 1RSB-type trial, push the best rigorous upper bound below 4.4898. That project is of theory interest only.
targets: random-SAT instance generators (SAT Competition random track; CNFgen / makewff-style tools)
first_step: Measure the 10–90% satisfiability window of random 3-SAT (clauses sampled with replacement) at n=50…2000 with a CDCL solver and check sqrt(n) clause-width scaling. Then correct generator documentation that quotes nu≈1.5.
caveats: Carenini (ECCC TR26-229) has priority on threshold existence. The window is in clause count at fixed probability levels and concerns satisfiability, not solver hardness. The k=3 Theta(n) variance paper is not formalized (Lean covers O(n log n) for k=3). Computability gives no usable digits.
evidence: /root/openai-math/preprints/Computing-the-Random-3-SAT-Threshold-September-27-2026/build/sections/introduction.tex (Thm thm:main); certificates.tex (Lemma cert:search); trials.tex (Lemma ctr:evaluation, Prop ctr:upper); probability.tex (Prop cp:finite-computation); proof-map.tex (2^67 n^{-1/6})

title: The exact factor-of-IID threshold for free Ising spins on trees
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: The free Ising state on the infinite d-regular tree can be produced from independent per-vertex random labels by a symmetric rule exactly when tanh(beta) <= 1/sqrt(d-1), which is the reconstruction (Kesten–Stigum) threshold.
constructive: no: a measurable, non-finitary factor. The paper explicitly asserts no finitary coding or coding-radius bound, and no parameter-uniform or computational bound.
explicit_constants: The threshold is exact. There is no radius or complexity bound.
opportunity: No operational channel. Factors of IID are the limit objects of local randomized (distributed/GNN) algorithms on random regular graphs. Without a coding-radius bound, the result yields no bounded-round distributed sampler and no limit on GNN design. The theoretical takeaway is that correlation-decay obstructions to local sampling of the free Ising state start at the reconstruction threshold, not at uniqueness.
caveats: Infinite tree, zero field, ferromagnetic only.

title: The three-quarter exponent for honeycomb self-avoiding walk
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: A uniformly random n-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice has diameter n^{3/4+o(1)}, matching Nienhuis's prediction for 2D polymers.
explicit_constants: No: o(1) exponent slack.
opportunity: None. The 2D Flory exponent 3/4 has long been accepted in polymer physics and is numerically confirmed to many digits. Rigour adds no new quantity.
caveats: Lean covers only supporting summability, free-energy and strip-crossing statements.

title: Optimal logarithmic mixing of the Thorp shuffle
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: The Thorp shuffle cuts the deck in half and randomly orders each pair of facing cards. It randomizes the entire order of N=2^d cards in Theta(log N) shuffles: 1600·log2 N shuffles suffice (Lean-verified), and about 2·log2 N are necessary.
constructive: yes: the shuffle is the algorithm. The result certifies a fixed-depth, oblivious random switching network, equivalently the round function of the Morris–Rogaway–Stegers small-domain cipher.
explicit_constants: Yes in the 1600d proof. Variants give 512d, 2048d and 32800d. Tracing constants: TV <= 8(1-M) + 0.5·sqrt(A^16·sum D^-3) with A=sqrt(32·C1), C1≈3.28, so TV ≈ 9e7·N^{-3/2} for large N: 3e-7 at N=2^32, 1e-21 at N=2^64. The companion bound 0.5·N^{-5} uses an unspecified absolute sweep count P.
opportunity: This is the first proof that a fixed-round (oblivious, constant-time) shuffle cipher is secure even against an adversary querying all N points, using Theta(lg N) rounds. Before, Thorp was proven only up to q < N/(4 lg N), or N^{1-1/r} queries with O(r lg N) rounds; full security in O(lg N) rounds needed the variable-time Sometimes-Recurse (SR) construction. It does not reduce rounds in practice. 1600·lg N rounds, doubled for CCA, is about 205k PRF calls per encryption at N=2^64, 100–200x more than swap-or-not/SR parameter sets of about 1000 rounds. It applies only to N=2^d, and its N^{-3/2} floor is weak exactly at FPE-sized domains (about 2^-19 at N=2^30). The reusable piece is the 'partial-permutation -> full law' Fourier transfer. It appears to turn Hoang–Morris–Rogaway's swap-or-not bound for 7N/8 fixed queries into full-permutation security with roughly 8x the rounds, qualitatively settling their full-security conjecture; that extrapolation is mine and unchecked.
targets: small-domain / format-preserving encryption research (Thorp/MRS, swap-or-not, Sometimes-Recurse: Rogaway, Hoang, Morris, Tessaro)
oblivious-shuffle / mixnet switching-network designs (Atom iterated butterfly; Czumaj O(log^2 n) networks)
first_step: Write the swap-or-not corollary: plug HMR Thm 3 at q=7N/8 into the eight-block Fourier lift (Prop orbit-lift / Thm l:main), using sign mean 0 and N divisible by 8, and tabulate concrete rounds against SR. In parallel, compute the exact TV of the Thorp shuffle for N=8 and empirical statistics for N=16–64 to estimate the true constant, which is somewhere in [2,1600].
caveats: Asymptotic in d. Powers of two only. The constant 1600 is a proof artifact, not a sharp value. The Fourier lift leaves a round-independent TV floor of about 1e8·N^{-3/2}. No deployed FPE standard uses Thorp (the Voltage-era patent US 8687802 exists). The swap-or-not transfer is an unverified extrapolation. Production oblivious shuffles (Waksman routing of a sampled permutation, bitonic sort) are already far cheaper.

title: Sharp singularity rates for symmetric random sign matrices
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: A random symmetric matrix of ±1 entries is singular with probability (1/2+o(1))^n. With biased signs the probability is (p^2+(1-p)^2+o(1))^n, dominated by two equal rows.
explicit_constants: No: o(1) in the exponential base, with no rate.
opportunity: None. Numerical linear algebra and compressed sensing care about conditioning (least singular value) and real-valued ensembles, not the exact singularity probability of sign matrices, which is about 2^-n at any n where the theorem says something beyond the trivial equal-rows bound.
caveats: Not formalized.
